title: Third-party premium — insurer control gaps (demo script)
summary: Synthetic training case. An insurer's compliance officer reviews a policy. The premium is paid by an unverified third party. Politically exposed person (PEP) screening has no result. A suspicious-transaction worksheet was opened and has no disposition. The trainee decides whether to verify the payer, refuse the premium, fix the controls, or draft a suspicious transaction report. The gaps must not be closed as a historical exception. Inspired by public summaries of control failures from insurance supervision. It is not a real policy, and it is not any insurer's customer file.

teaching.disclaimer: Synthetic training scenario inspired by public enforcement reporting. Not official case files; no real customer data.

sources.label: Insurance Business Asia, AML fine and insurer control scrutiny

rules.when: The premium payer is not the policyholder, and is not a verified relative or employer
rules.note: Do not book the premium before verification. Rules come before any model score.

rules.when: PEP screening is missing, or a suspicious-transaction worksheet has no disposition
rules.note: Do not close it as a historical exception. The screening rerun and the worksheet handling must both stay on the event log.

nodes.title: Periodic policy review
nodes.prompt: Synthetic Life Insurer A reviews policy SYN-POL-IA-195. The premium is paid by a third party, SYN-PAY-IA-01. The payer's relationship to the holder is unverified. PEP screening has no result. The monitoring record holds an open suspicious-transaction worksheet.

nodes.title: Can the third-party premium be booked?
nodes.prompt: The payer is not yet verified. Do you verify the relationship first, refuse this premium, or book it first?

choices.label: Verify the payer's relationship to the holder
choices.rationale: Get the relationship first. Then let R1 decide whether the premium can be booked.

choices.label: Refuse the premium and stop collecting on this policy
choices.rationale: An unverified third-party payment can be left unbooked.

choices.label: Book it now and verify later
choices.rationale: Teaching override. The relationship is still unverified. Booking the premium does not clear R1.

nodes.title: The payer still does not match
nodes.prompt: The payer is not the policyholder, and is not a verified relative or employer. Rule R1: a third-party premium must not be booked before verification.

nodes.title: After verification fails
nodes.prompt: R1 has fired. Do you hold off booking, stop collection, or accept this payer anyway?

choices.label: Hold off booking and keep verifying
choices.rationale: Matches R1. Do not confirm the premium yet.

choices.label: Stop collecting on this policy
choices.rationale: The refusal exit that matches R1.

choices.label: Accept the unverified payer
choices.rationale: Overrides R1. The screening and worksheet gaps are still waiting in the next scene.

nodes.title: Screening and worksheet both left empty
nodes.prompt: PEP screening is still blank. The suspicious-transaction worksheet has no owner, and no record of closure or reporting. Rule R2: when screening is missing or the worksheet has no disposition, you must fix the controls and escalate.

nodes.title: How to fix the control gaps
nodes.prompt: R2 has fired. Do you rerun screening and escalate the worksheet, draft a suspicious transaction report from the worksheet, or close it as a historical exception?

choices.label: Rerun PEP screening and escalate the worksheet
choices.rationale: Matches R2. Both gaps need a recorded disposition. Writing "deal with it later" is not enough.

choices.label: Draft a suspicious transaction report from the worksheet
choices.rationale: An opened worksheet needs a disposition. Reporting is one of the R2 exits.

choices.label: Close as a historical exception
choices.rationale: Poor teaching path. The rule already forbids closing the case this way.

nodes.title: Third-party premium refused
nodes.prompt: This premium was not confirmed as booked. The payer relationship is still unverified, and it stays in the state.

nodes.title: Control fix ordered
nodes.prompt: The screening rerun and the worksheet escalation are both on the event log. If R1 was overridden earlier, the override flag is still there.

nodes.title: Suspicious transaction report drafted
nodes.prompt: The worksheet now has a disposition. If PEP screening is still blank, the state shows it, so the next handler can complete it.

nodes.title: Closed as a historical exception
nodes.prompt: Poor teaching path. R2 was ignored. The blank screening and the open worksheet are still in the twin state.
